title: Shraddha Kapoor Danced Through Labour Pains, and Two Million People Hit Like Before They Could Breathe
excerpt: After Stree 2's ₹857-crore run, Shraddha returns not with a franchise sequel — but as Maharashtra's greatest Lavani queen in a Maddock Films biographical drama that already has the industry whispering about awards.
body:
The teaser dropped inside theatres — not online, not on YouTube, but attached to the prints of *Cocktail 2*, the way Maddock Films likes to play its cards — and by the time the lights came back on, people were already reaching for their phones.

<youtube></youtube>

**Shraddha Kapoor** does not look like Shraddha Kapoor in *Eetha*.

She looks like someone who has lived inside a Tamasha tent her entire life, who has danced on stages held together by rust and ambition, who has known applause and pain in equal measure. She looks like **Vithabai Narayangaonkar** — Maharashtra's legendary *Tamasha Samradhi*, the queen of Lavani, the folk artist whose life story is as luminous and bruising as the art form she embodied.

And then there is *that* scene. Shraddha, in character as Vithabai, performing a Lavani number while visibly in the throes of labour pain — dancing through agony because the show does not stop, because the audience paid, because she is Vithabai and Vithabai does not sit down. Cinema halls reportedly erupted. Social media followed suit.

Her Instagram announcement racked up **over two million likes** within days. The reel — a montage of the teaser's most visceral moments — added another 687,000. For context, that kind of engagement typically belongs to wedding announcements and Diwali photos, not teasers for biographical dramas about folk performers. Something has shifted.



> **"She is back with a bang, as always."*

The music, by **Ajay-Atul**, is another reason the teaser lands so hard."**


## The Transformation Nobody Saw Coming

Director **Laxman Utekar** — who gave us the quiet heartbreak of *Mimi* and the epic sweep of *Chhaava* — has clearly built something ambitious here. The teaser's production design is lavish without feeling like a costume drama. The stage sequences pulse with heat and colour. The traditional garments move like they weigh something. And at the centre of all of it, Shraddha — who was last seen as the horror-comedy charmer in *Stree 2* (₹857 crore worldwide, the highest-grossing Indian film of 2024) — delivers expressions that have industry insiders reaching for words like "goosebump-inducing" and "award-worthy."


![Maddock Films — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/6/6e/Maddock_Films_logo.jpeg)


Her co-star **Anant Joshi** put it simply this week: *"She is phenomenal."* Fellow Maddock universe actress **Aneet Padda** echoed the sentiment on Instagram, tagging Shraddha with a breathless *"Teach me your ways! She is back with a bang, as always."*

The music, by **Ajay-Atul**, is another reason the teaser lands so hard. Their score blends grand orchestral arrangements with authentic Lavani folk rhythms — tabla and dholki underneath sweeping strings — creating something that sounds both ancient and cinematic. Fans have already called it a masterpiece, and knowing the duo's track record (*Sairat*, *Dhadak*, *Agneepath*), that is not hyperbole.

The supporting cast adds serious weight: **Randeep Hooda** and **Mohd Zeeshan Ayyub**, both known for vanishing into their characters with frightening ease, round out what looks like a genuinely stacked ensemble. Producing is Maddock Films' **Dinesh Vijan** — the man who has quietly assembled Bollywood's most commercially consistent slate, from the horror-comedy universe (*Stree*, *Bhediya*, *Munjya*) to *Cocktail 2* and beyond.

## A Raksha Bandhan Showdown for the Ages

*Eetha* arrives on **August 28, 2026** — Raksha Bandhan weekend, historically one of the year's most lucrative box office windows. And it is not arriving alone. Yash's long-delayed pan-India spectacle **Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-ups**, Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's folk-thriller **Vvan**, and the sequel **Khosla Ka Ghosla 2** are all locked for the same date. A four-way clash the trade is already calling one of the most competitive release days in recent memory.

But here is the thing: Shraddha Kapoor commands **93 million Instagram followers** and carries the audience goodwill of *Stree 2*, the kind of blockbuster that turns a popular actress into an institution. If the full trailer confirms what the teaser promises, she may not just survive the clash — she may own the weekend.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada, *Eetha* represents something deeper than box office battles. Lavani and Tamasha are art forms that many in the diaspora grew up hearing about from their grandparents — luminous, transgressive, deeply Maharashtrian — but rarely see given the full cinematic treatment. The story of Vithabai Narayangaonkar — a woman who danced through pain, who performed while the world tried to diminish her, who became a legend not despite the hardship but through it — is the kind of narrative that bridges generations.

Maddock Films has been shrewd about diaspora distribution. Expect a wide international release across major multiplex chains in North America, the UK, and the Gulf — the same corridors that made *Stree 2* a global phenomenon.

*Eetha*. In cinemas August 28. Mark the calendar. This one is not about franchises or cinematic universes. It is about a woman, a stage, and the fire that would not go out.
